name: scatter_ho
description: Ho — a language of the Munda people of the Chotanagpur plateau (Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal), closely related to Mundari and Santali; written in its own Warang Citi script as well as Devanagari, Odia, Bengali, and Roman; sister languages include Mundari, Santali, Korku, Sora — on the standardized 12-column place axis. Voiceless / voiced stop pairs across 5 places (bilabial, dental, retroflex, palatal, velar). Four matched nasals (m, n, ɲ, ŋ). The 'checked' (glottalized) stops of Ho and its sister languages are word-final allophones of the regular stops, not separate phonemes — they don't appear as distinct cells here. Sibilant /s/, glottal /h/, lateral /l/, retroflex flap /ɽ/, trill /r/, glides /w, j/. Conservative inventory drawn from Anderson & Osada (2008); some sources also list voiceless-aspirated stops in Indic loans (not shown here, to keep the cells phonemic). 21 cells filled.
